intro: Looking after the mouth is essential daily personal care; a clean, comfortable mouth supports eating, comfort, dignity and general health.
points: Good daily mouth care reduces harmful bacteria and helps protect people prone to aspiration from aspiration pneumonia.
Never force mouth care; where someone lacks capacity, give it in their best interests under the Mental Capacity Act.
This e-learning covers knowledge only; assessing, diagnosing and treating the mouth is always the dentist's role, not yours.
Brush natural teeth twice daily with a small soft brush and fluoride toothpaste, then spit, don't rinse.
Clean dentures daily over water with a denture brush, not toothpaste, and leave them out overnight.
Report ulcers lasting about three weeks, thrush, bleeding or ill-fitting dentures; never adjust a denture yourself.
